# Add exploration-log, generated by running skill-scaffold for real

- **Commit:** `5919cb8edb9e2b2aae6fa06930c1350e97c74b11` (`5919cb8`)
- **Author:** Claude
- **Date:** 2026-08-16

## Commit message

The first execution of skill-scaffold, against a real target rather than a
throwaway. exploration-log writes design/explorations/ -- the tier the
design thesis rests on and the one no design tool has: a durable record of
the directions that were tried and killed, and why.

Git solves this for code by accident; the rejected approach stays in the
history whether you wanted it or not. Design has no equivalent -- the
alternative is deleted from the file and gone.

Two modes, because a tier that can only be written to is worthless:
capture (log a round: what it tested, what changed, what was learned,
kept/killed/parked with the reason) and retrieval (answer "have we tried
this?" with the round, the verdict and the quote).

No CLAUDE.md protocol block: skill:design-setup already states "a killed
direction is never deleted", and a second block asserting the same rule is
the drift the marker convention exists to prevent.

Also fixes a README/skills.ts divergence found during the run -- "Working
conventions" and "Build the skills themselves" had a note in skills.ts and
none in the README.
